Candidate_Claim: The locked test set was isolated from model development.
Empirical_Evidence: Pairwise patient intersection is strictly 0; locked test was never passed to training dataloaders.

Candidate_Claim: Canonical locked-test results are traceable to frozen checkpoints selected using validation criteria.
Empirical_Evidence: All 9 checkpoints match recorded SHA-256 hashes and restore epochs of peak validation performance.

Candidate_Claim: ResNet18 Protocol A achieved 97.34% accuracy and 0.9830 ROC-AUC on the locked test.
ResNet18 Protocol A achieved 75% LGG Recall on the locked test.
Empirical_Evidence: Directly calculated as 9 of 12 locked-test LGG patients correctly classified.

Candidate_Claim: The 75% LGG Recall should be interpreted as universally representative performance.
Empirical_Evidence: Cross-validation reveals that average expected sensitivity across development partitions is 50.55% +/- 32.74%.

Candidate_Claim: Five-fold CV revealed substantial variability in LGG sensitivity.
Empirical_Evidence: Phase 6 CV LGG Recall ranged from 0.00% to 80.00% across 5 stratified folds (SD = 32.74%).

Candidate_Claim: Overall discrimination was substantially more stable than minority-class sensitivity.
Patient partitioning contributes to observed minority-class variability.
Empirical_Evidence: Identical training pipeline produced 0% recall in Fold 4 and 80% recall in Fold 5 under different patient subsets.

Candidate_Claim: Patient partitioning is the sole cause of the variability.
Empirical_Evidence: Patient distribution is a major contributor, but optimization dynamics and early stopping rules also interact.

Candidate_Claim: Training stochasticity is the primary cause of variability.
Empirical_Evidence: Multi-seed fixed-split training has not been decoupled from patient partition variance.

Candidate_Claim: Static class weighting universally improves minority detection.
Empirical_Evidence: Directly contradicted in 6 of 9 project configurations on the controlled benchmark.
CNN sensitivity declined under weighting, while SwinUNETR sensitivity improved under Protocol C.

Candidate_Claim: Threshold optimization can recover minority sensitivity in some configurations.
Empirical_Evidence: Validation-tuned tau* increased SwinUNETR Prot A recall from 0% to 100% and ResNet18 recall from 75% to 91.7%.
ROC-AUC is invariant to threshold shifts; thresholding moves along the existing ROC curve.
Threshold tuning alters decision cutoffs but leaves predicted probability distributions (ECE, Brier) unchanged.
Sensitivity gains are accompanied by increased majority false positives; clinical preference depends on utility costs.

Candidate_Claim: Focal Loss will solve the minority-class instability.
Empirical_Evidence: Unproven hypothesis; Focal Loss has not yet been experimentally trained or evaluated on this pipeline.

Candidate_Claim: Focal Loss is a scientifically justified next experiment.
Empirical_Evidence: Motivated by evidence that static class weighting fails to down-weight easy majority examples dynamically.
